summary: KERNEL CONTEST: The legal threshold of personhood (the codified or common-law kernel) read restrictively to exclude nascent or non-human entities (e.g., fetuses, ecosystems, or AI) versus read expansively to grant them rights and legal standing. Each reading emits constraints with radically different victim and beneficiary sets, making this a canonical contested present boundary[cite: 2, 3].

KERNEL CONTEST: The legendary laws of Lycurgus (the foundational Spartan commitment system) read as a sacred, unchangeable code requiring absolute adherence (where the authority structure completely denies revision), versus read historically as a brittle trap that caused demographic collapse. A pristine example of a commitment system where drift is absent and revision is forbidden[cite: 2, 3].

KERNEL CONTEST: A state's constitutional framework (the shared legal kernel) read as establishing parliamentary/legislative sovereignty (where elected bodies hold ultimate interpretive authority) versus read as subordinate to a supreme judiciary or unwritten fundamental rights. This contest dictates who possesses the legitimate authority to adjudicate state coercion.

KERNEL CONTEST: The legal designation of 'beta' software (a codified industry/legal norm) read expansively by developers as a blanket shield against liability and accountability (an extractive Snare) versus read narrowly by regulators as a temporary consumer warning (a Scaffold). Competing readings of the exact same label yield entirely different jurisdictional boundaries[cite: 2, 3].
